## Completion Report

All 52 tasks in `tasks.md` are complete and marked `[X]`. **196 tests pass**, every one of FR-001…FR-044 is named by at least one of them.

**What was built** — 4 runtime modules, 680 lines, standard library only:

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `src/pastebin/__init__.py` | version constant |
| `src/pastebin/__main__.py` | `argparse` CLI, storage preparation, bind, the one ready line |
| `src/pastebin/server.py` | routing, body limits, validation, JSON responses |
| `src/pastebin/store.py` | records on disk, atomic publication, lazy expiry |

Plus `README.md`, `pytest.ini`, `requirements-dev.txt`, and 10 test modules organised by requirement group.

**Verification beyond the suite:**
- All seven quickstart scenarios run against a live service and matched their stated expectations — including the `nc` oversize-declared-body case (immediate `413`), the quiet-connection case (an unrelated read served in 1.3 ms while a caller held a connection open), restart durability (`expires_at` unchanged, original token still valid, a snippet that expired while stopped gone), and all four startup failures with the right exit statuses (`2`, `2`, `1`, `1`) and no ready line.
- Constitution gate audited mechanically: no third-party import in any runtime module; no bare `except`, no `except Exception`, no handler that only passes, every handler naming an exception from research.md R-08; no directory enumeration anywhere (`iterdir`/`listdir`/`scandir`/`glob`/`walk` absent), no module-level cache or index; 2 CLI options, 2 classes, no env vars, no abstract bases.
- Output contract checked end to end: across 18 valid and invalid requests, stdout held exactly the one ready line and stderr only the single damaged-storage diagnostic.

**One design addition beyond the plan.** Live validation revealed a real FR-044/SC-009 defect the task list didn't anticipate: when a caller resets its connection, `socketserver` prints a traceback to stderr. I reproduced it in three distinct places (response write, body read, and inside `http.server`'s own `handle_one_request`), so I added a `Server(ThreadingHTTPServer)` subclass whose `handle_error` returns silently for connection-level errors only — `BrokenPipeError`, `ConnectionResetError`, `ConnectionAbortedError`, `TimeoutError` — and defers to the standard loud traceback for anything else. Wrapping call sites would have left the request-line read uncovered, and reimplementing `handle_one_request` is what research.md R-08 rejects. Two tests lock both halves down: `test_fr044_stderr_silent_when_a_caller_abandons_the_connection` (4 abandonment patterns) and `test_unanticipated_failure_is_still_loud`. Research R-08's exception table has no row for a vanished peer — worth adding there if you want the docs to match the code.

**Two smaller notes:**
- The TDD gate was honoured by rolling the runtime modules back to the Phase 2 shell after I got ahead of myself, then reintroducing each story's code once its tests existed and failed: 53/54 red before US1, 21 red before US2, 7 red before US3. US4's tests passed on arrival, which T039 explicitly anticipated — the US1 storage contract already satisfies the restart requirements.
- `src/pastebin/__main__.py` installs a SIGTERM handler so an interrupt exits `0` as `contracts/cli.md` requires. Note that a non-interactive shell starts background jobs with SIGINT ignored, so `kill -INT` on a backgrounded service does nothing — use SIGTERM there (this bit me twice during validation, not a service defect).
